_what_this_is: A DAMAGE RECORD, not an exception list. Each entry states a known, measured,
permanent hole in the RECORDED store, with enough detail that anyone can
re-derive it from the public archive without trusting this file.
It is consulted by exactly one assertion: COMPLETENESS (archive \ recorded).
It is NEVER consulted for FIDELITY. If the collector invents a print, or
disagrees with the venue on any field of any print it did record, the gate
goes red and this file offers no way out. Completeness may carry a labelled
The completeness assertion matches the EXACT SET of missing ids against the
id_ranges below. A single print of new loss fails the gate. This file cannot
be used to wave through damage it does not already name to the print.
Every field in _required_fields is enforced by test_damage_record_is_a_record
so this cannot decay into a bare list of dates.

entries.utc_hour_profile: 100% in UTC 00-07 (off hours). 0% in UTC 16-22 (NY session, the best-coverage window). 70.6 min of tape = 4.91% of the day.
entries.cause: aggTrades cursor reset on leg restart. _aggtrades_loop initialised `cursor: Optional[int] = None` per call (collector.py:2744 @ 57ad311), so a leg restart inside a live process resumed at the LIVE EDGE and silently dropped the backlog accumulated during the outage. The `cursor is not None` guard at :2754 suppressed the id-gap alarm that would have announced it. Attribution rests on the shape: all four holes are perfectly CONTIGUOUS id blocks, which is what jump-to-live-edge produces and what packet loss or a venue outage does not.

entries.cause: HOST REBOOT at 22:23:38Z (ordered shutdown; kern.boottime). The aggTrades cursor was module-scope (in-memory) only — the cross-process sidecar (data/ticks/aggtrades-cursor.json) was created ~4.5 h AFTER this window — so the relaunched process seeded from the live edge. Outages under ~90 s lose nothing (the bare seed poll returns the last 1,000 rows and dedup drops re-served ids — measured: the 00:05:28Z kickstart restart on this same day left ZERO hole); this 6.7 min outage exceeded that page depth.
